question: Which semantic objects own the blocked frontier of the real branch-8 remove-then-reroute failure, and are those identities stable enough to drive later mixed placement/routing actions?

identity_rules.footprint_pad: group all matching pad obstacles by stable footprint reference and retain the union of their foreign nets
identity_rules.foreign_net_copper: group segments and vias by normalized KiCad net name
identity_rules.component_mobility: true only when the owning footprint declares Router_Movable=yes

implementation.counting_rule: one blocker receives at most one hit per blocked frontier cell even if several of its pad/track primitives cover that cell
implementation.diagnostic_overlay: the twelve highest-hit blockers are labeled at their frontier centroids; movable pads are green, fixed pads orange, and foreign nets violet
implementation.transaction_rule: semantic diagnostics do not make the invalid topology-only candidate selectable

cross_resolution_interpretation.front: all three resolutions identify the same nine blockers in the same leading structure: fixed J4 first, then D_EN and D_LOCAL_COMM0; movable C4 and R19 are visible but cannot explain the whole cut
cross_resolution_interpretation.back: T_EN and GND are the two leading blockers at every resolution, followed by T_BUS_RELAY0 and T_LOCAL_FLEX1; low-hit tail nets vary with raster resolution
cross_resolution_interpretation.coverage: all 2596 frontier cells across the six searches were attributed to at least one semantic owner

worked: the KiCad adapter no longer discards obstacle identity when rasterizing pads, tracks, and vias
frontier ownership is complete on the real control and stable for the dominant blockers across all three resolutions
component mobility comes from the existing board declaration instead of being inferred from geometry
the reduced regression proves per-cell deduplication, movable-component attribution, serialization, and visible SVG labels; the real-board regression checks J4, C4, and D_EN
limits: frontier-hit count measures encountered boundary pressure, not a causal minimum cut; removing the highest-hit object alone is not proven sufficient
foreign copper is grouped by net because the generated KiCad board has no durable per-branch identity for those nets
the set of low-hit back-layer blockers changes with raster resolution, so mixed-action generation should prioritize cross-resolution persistence rather than raw fine-grid count alone
GND is treated as ordinary routed copper for now; future ground zones will materially change its geometry and action policy
this step diagnoses mixed actions but does not yet generate, evaluate, or commit them
critical_evaluation.next: add a replaceable mixed-action producer that uses persistent semantic blockers to try bounded foreign-net rip-up/reroute and declared component motion before re-running the target local repair, while preserving the source as the always-valid fallback
